4000:
** πεντᾰκισ-χίλιοι** [χῑ], αι, α,
**five thousand**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.194, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 738a: in _sing._, π. ἀσπίς}} **five thousand** men-at-arms, {{LXX+2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMeretr.” 9.4; π. ἵππος LXX 1 LXX.Mal.4.28}}:—_Doric dialect_ form **πεντακιχήλιοι** {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“Abh.Berl.Akad.” 1925(5).25 (Cyrene, 3rd c.BC).}}
4002:
** πέντε**,
_Aeolic dialect_ **πέμπε** (which see), οἱ, αἱ, τά, _indeclinable_ (declined in _Aeolic dialect_), **five**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.317, etc.}}; τὰ πέντε κρατήσας having won the πένταθλον, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 155.11. (I.- 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus}} **penq[uglide]e**, cf. Sanskrit _páñca_, Lithuanian _penki_, etc. 'five'.)
4003:
** πεντεκαι-δέκᾰτος**, η, ον,
**fifteenth**, {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 941b14, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 12.81, NT.Luke.3.1; π. τόκοι “Supp.epigram” 4.664.17 (Ilium, 1st c.BC).}}
4004:
** πεντήκοντα**, οἱ, αἱ, τά,
_indeclinable_, **fifty**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.509, etc.}}: _Boeotian dialect_ **πεντείκοντα** {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.67: _genitive_ _plural_ πεντηκόντων “Schwyzer” 688 D 7 (Chios, 5th c.BC).}}
4006:
** πεποίθ-ησις**, εως, ἡ,
**trust, confidence, boldness**, {{LXX+1st c.BC+|LXX.2Ki.18.19, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.22 O., 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.444, NT.Eph.3.12, 3rd c.AD: Philumenus Medicus “de Venenatis Animalibus” 2.4; π. ἐπὶ τῇ δυνάμει 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 1.3.1; ἡ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ π. [prev. work] 10.1.4}}: in _plural_, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 43.19.}}
4010:
1. **Pergamus **, the citadel of Troy, {{8th/7th c.BC|Iliad by Homer}}; τὸ Πριάμου Πέργαμον {{Refs 5th c.BC|Herdotus Historicus}}; τὰ Πέργαμα [{{Refs 5th c.BC|Sophocles Tragicus}}, {{Refs 5th c.BC|Euripides}}], etc.: —;then, any **citadel **, [{{6th/5th c.BC|Aeschulus Tragicus}}, {{Refs 5th c.BC|Euripides}}]
2. also Περγαμία, {{Refs 5th c.BC|Pindar}} (Middle Liddel)
4011:
**Πέργη**, -ης, ἡ
**Perga, a city of Pamphylia**: Act.13:13-14 14:25.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
4024:
** περι-ζώννυμι**,
**gird upon** a person, π. τὸ ξίφος [τινί] {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 6.9.4, compare 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Ἀννιβαϊκή” 20, 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 40.460 (probable reading)}}; **gird**, τὸ παιδίον probably in {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus (?) 20.1}}:—more frequently in _middle_ with _perfect_ _passive_, **gird oneself with**, ᾤαν λουτρίδα Theopomp. Comedy texts {{Refs|37}}; ἐσθῆτα, τήβεννον, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Romulus” 16, “Cor.” 9}}; γυμνὸς ὢν τοῦτον τὸν ἄνδρα περιεζώσατο **put** him **on** as a defence, παρ᾽ ὑπόνοιαν for ἐπίτροπον ἐποιήσατο, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 687}}; περιεζῶσθαι τὴν φορβειάν **to have** their halter **girded round them.** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1324b16: with _dative_, - ζώσασθαι τοῖς ἐντέροις τινός 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.26 W.: _absolutely_, Κλέων.. περιζωσάμενος ἐδημηγόρησε 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 28.3; π. κοσμίως ἄνωθεν καὶ κάτωθεν 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.70a}}; of a cook, περιεζωσμένος **with his apron on**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 174.11, compare 4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 41.12 (_anapaest meter_); αἱ νῆτται περιεζωσμέναι ἐπλινθοφόρουν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1148}}; of athletes, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.44.1}}; of a dancer, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 30.22.10.}}
4025:
** περί-θεσις**, εως, ἡ,
**putting round, putting on**, ἐκ περιθέσεως in the act of **application**, Heraclasap. {{NT+1st c.AD+|4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 48.12.1; π. χρυσίων NT.1Pet.3.3; βρόχου 3rd c.AD: Philumenus Medicus “de Venenatis Animalibus” 7.8; στραγγάλης 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 3.15: _plural_, π. πλοκαμίδων 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 19.1.5; κωνωπίων 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.85.}}
4031:
** περικρᾰτ-ής**, ές,
**grasping, tenacious**, γαμφηλαί {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Simmias 1.11}}; **having full command over**, π. γενέσθαι τῆς σκάφης {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.Act.27.16, compare 2nd c.AD(?): Theodotion LXX “Su.” 39 (variant)}}; compare περικρεμής.
4032:
** περικρύπτω**,
late _imperfect_ -έκρυβον {{NT|NT.Luke.1.24}}: — **conceal entirely**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 10.8, 4th-5th c.AD: Eunapius Historicus “Fragmenta Historica - HGM” p.248 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, etc.}}:—_middle_, **conceal oneself from**, τινα {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 6.61.}}
4035:
** περιλείπομαι**,
_middle_ and _passive_, **remain over, survive**, ὅσσοι δ᾽ ἂν πολέμοιο περὶ στυγεροῖο λίπωνται {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.230; τὸν περιλειφθέντα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.82; ὑπὸ τῶν κόρεων εἴ μού τι περιλειφθήσεται 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 725; τοὺς περιλελειμμένους φίλων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 426, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 23c (_passive_), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Oeconomica” 1350a29, etc.}}
4036:
** περίλῡπ-ος**, ον,
**very sad, deeply grieved**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 42}}; opposed to περιχαρής, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.42, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1124a16}}; στυγνὸς καὶ π. {{LXX+4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demades Orator 17, cf. LXX.Gen.4.6, +others}}
4039:
** περιοικ-έω**,
(περίοικος) **dwell round** persons or places, with _accusative_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.57, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.16: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.23, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.28}}:—_passive_, **to be inhabited all round**, κύκλῳ {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 354a4, 4th c.BC(?): Scylax Geographus 107, 2nd c.BC: Scymnus Geographus 766.}}
4058:
** περιστερ-ά**, ἡ,
**common pigeon** or **dove**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.138, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 866, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 164, etc.}}; specifically, **Columba livia domestica**, and so distinguished from φάψ, φάττα, οἰνάς, τρυγών, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 562b5, 593a16; ἐλάττων μὲν ἡ πελειάς, τιθασὸν δὲ γίνεται μᾶλλον ἡ π. [prev. work] 544b3}}: **περιστερός**, ὁ, **cock-pigeon**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 33}} (of a carrier-**pigeon**), {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 214; censured by 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sol.” 7.}}
4066:
** περίχωρ-ος**, ον,
**round about a place**: οἱ π. **the people about**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.266, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Ma.” 25, “Eum.” 15, etc.}}; ἡ π. (i.e. γῆ) **the country round about**, {{LXX+NT|LXX.Gen.13.10, +others, NT.Matt.14.35}}; τὰ π. {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Palaephatus Paradoxographus 20.}}
4067:
** περίψ-ημα**, ατος, τό,
**anything wiped off, offscouring**, of a vile person (or **scapegoat**), {{NT+9th c.AD+|NT.1Cor.4.13, 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.}}; π. σου your **humble servant**, {{Refs|“CIL” 8.12924 (from Carthage), “LW” 2493 (from Syria), “Classical Studies in honor of J.C.Rolfe” 318 (from Ostia)}}; **peripsuma su** (sic), Dessau {{Refs|“ILS” 5725 (from Brixia).}}
4068:
** περπερ-εύομαι**,
**boast, brag**, {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.1Cor.13.4, 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 5.5.}}
4070:
** πέρῠσι**,
before a vowel **πέρυσιν**, _Aeolic dialect_ **πέρρυσι** {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 29.26}}, _Doric dialect_ **πέρυτι** {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 50.19}}: _adverb_:— **a year ago, last year**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 75, 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 76, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1038, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 17.5, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 327d, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 731, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.98; ἡ π. κωμῳδία 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 378}}; ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν οἱ αὐτοὶ νῦν τε καὶ π. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.7}}; ἀπὸ π. {{NT|NT.2Cor.8.10}}. (Cf. Sanskrit _parút_, Armenian _heru_, MHG. **vert** 'last year'.)
4071:
** πετεινός**, ή, όν,
also **πετηνός** (see. near the end), and **πτηνός** (see. entry), _Epic dialect_ and _poetry_ **πετεηνός** (also **πετεεινός** {{Refs 1st c.BC+|“Anthologia Graeca” 9.337 (1st c.AD: Leonidas Alexandrinus Epigrammaticus), 363.22 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus))}}:— **able to fly, full-fledged**, of young birds, πάρος πετεηνὰ γενέσθαι {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.218}}; of birds generally, **able to fly, winged**, πετηνῶν.. ὑπ᾽ οἰωνῶν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1025; πετηνοῖς γυψί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 515; also π. ἵππος 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 342: _absolutely_, πετεηνά}} **winged fowl**, αἰετὸς.. τελειότατος πετεηνῶν {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.247, +others}}; πετεινόν **a bird**, {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1097}}; τὰ πετεινά (with variant{πετηνά}) {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.140, 2.123, 3.106, 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 132.—Thom.Mag. p.272 R. rejects the form πετεινός: Πετηνή}} is the name of an _Attic dialect_ship in {{Refs|“IG” 22.1611.138.}}
4075:
** πετρ-ώδης**, ες,
**like rock** or **stone, rocky, stony**, π. κατῶρυξ, of a grave, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 774, compare 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Antro Nympharum - Porphyrii Opuscula” 9}}; of ground, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 1; γεηρὰ καὶ πετρώδη καὶ ἄγρια 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 612a; ἐν τοῖς τραχέσι καὶ πετρώδεσι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 549b14}}; τὸ π. {{Refs|“BMus.Inscription” 3.407.8 (from Priene)}}; ἄνθρωποι π. καὶ δενδρώδεις {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|Heraclitus Paradoxographus “de incredibilibus - Mythographi Graeci” 23; π. κεφαλή 3rd c.AD: Philumenus Medicus “de Venenatis Animalibus” 15.4.}}
4076:
** πήγᾰνον**, τό,
**rue, Ruta graveolens**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|Diocl.fragment 138, 4th c.BC: Theopompus Historicus 177 (a), 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 127.8, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.3.4, +others, 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 413}}; π. ὀρεινόν, ἄγριον, **mountain rue, Ruta halepensis**, [{{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.45 (but π. ἄγριον, ={μῶλυ}, [prev. work]46): proverbial, οὐδ᾽ ἐν δελίνῳ οὐδ᾽ ἐν πηγάνῳ}}], i.e. scarcely at the **edge** or **beginning** of a thing, because these herbs were planted for borders in gardens, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 480}}; compare περίκηπος.
4082:
** πήρα**,
_Ionic dialect_ **πήρη **(πάρη [ᾰ] {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Heraclides Historicus cited in 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 29.3)}}, ἡ, **leathern pouch** for victuals, etc., **wallet**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.437, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 298, “fragment” 273, “Ostr.Bodl.” iii 264 (1st c.AD), etc.}}
4086:
** πῐθᾰνο-λογία**, ἡ,
**use of probable arguments**, opposed to demonstration (ἀπόδειξις), {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 162e, cf. NT.Col.2.4, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 17(1).619.}}

4093:
** πῐνᾰκ-ίδιον** [κῐ], τό,
={πινάκιον}, {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 6.8.7, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mirabilia” 834b12, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Symmachus LXX.Eze.9.2, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.855}}; **writing-tablet**, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Eumenes” 1.}}
